title: Parsing an aligned pair of input bits
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $x,pre,rest$ be Boolean words, let $b,c$ be Booleans, and suppose $x=pre\mathbin{++}[b,c]\mathbin{++}rest$. Starting with the parsing state at input position $|pre|+1$, first buffer $a$, empty second buffer, first-buffer head at $|a|$, second-buffer head at $0$, and empty output, after two steps the machine is in the parsing state with the pair appended to the first buffer if $b=c$; if $b\ne c$ and $b$ is true, it has halted with the first buffer unchanged; and if $b\ne c$ and $b$ is false, it is in the copy state with the first-buffer head at $|a|-1$. In every case the input head is at position $|pre|+3$, the second buffer remains empty, and the output remains empty.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
